question.text: A portfolio manager forecasts that mid-caps will outperform in the next quarter. She buys NIFTY Midcap 100 futures instead of mid-cap stocks. This strategy primarily provides:

answer.text: Leveraged exposure enabling larger alpha for small margin

explanation.text: The Logic: Futures require margin (~10-15%), giving leveraged exposure — small capital delivers large notional, amplifying both alpha and downside. The Trap: Futures have higher (not lower) risk per rupee invested; they don't pay dividends; short-term gains are fully taxable as business income for PMS. Cross-Exam Context: VIII has this framing; XXI-B applies it to alpha-generation decisions. Manager's Pro-Tip: Match the contract's maturity to your view horizon — rolling futures monthly eats basis and is rarely free.
